summary.headline: Ddev Plastiks Q2 FY27 revenue rose 44% YoY to about INR970 crores, with EBITDA up 16% to INR86 crores at a 9% margin.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 44% YoY to about INR970 crores, led by Wires & Cable and rising exports, while EBITDA rose 16% to INR86 crores and PAT rose 10% to INR52 crores. H1 revenue was INR1,968 crores (+36%), EBITDA about INR187 crores (+22%) and PAT INR116 crores (+17%). Management raised the FY27 revenue estimate to INR3,800 crores from INR3,340 crores on higher realisations, while utilisation fell to about 63% from 81% as new PVC and XLPE capacity came on stream. Volume was about 102,000 MT in H1 against an earlier internal estimate of about 230,000 MT for the year, which management says must come in H2.

financial_highlights.change: Sep-25 quarter about INR15,500; FY26 average about INR15,700

financial_highlights.value: More than INR100 crores cash vs INR67 crores debt, net cash about INR35 crores

segments.name: Wires & Cable / Polymer compounds
segments.commentary: Management said the segment grew robustly and that PVC compound growth came from new customers in building wires. XLPE is the main revenue and margin driver.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export share was 29% of H1 sales versus about 25% last fiscal year. Management guides volume share to 30-plus% and value share above 25% or near 30%, with export margins usually a couple of percent better than domestic.

segments.name: HFFR compounds
segments.commentary: Existing HFFR capacity is being qualified with customers. The company plans to double HFFR capacity to about 20,000 tons by year-end, with new capacity aimed at already-approved products.

segments.name: BESS (battery storage)
segments.commentary: Still under construction and not yet live. Management targets go-live by end-FY27 or Q1 FY28, pending the state incentive policy notified on 5 November 2026. Revenue is excluded from the INR5,000 crore FY30 target.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue estimate raised to about INR3,800 crores from INR3,340 crores, on average realisation of about INR190 plus versus INR150 earlier.
FY27 EBITDA estimate of about INR360 crores maintained; management says actuals are on track.
Volume growth guidance of 10-15% for FY27 is unchanged, though H1 volume growth was only about 1-2%; H2 expected to carry the year.
Long-term target of INR5,000 crores revenue by FY30 is from the compounding business only, at lower realisations than now; BESS is additional.
EBITDA per ton benchmark of INR14,000 to INR17,000 is kept; management wants this tracked rather than EBITDA margin %.
FY27 capex guidance about INR175 crores; FY28 capex about INR50-70 crores. Next year revenue could be at least 10% above INR3,800 crores with volume growth and normalised prices.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 3.16 lakh tons; utilisation fell to about 63% from 81% a year earlier, as new PVC and XLPE capacity was added in FY26 and up to May 2026.
Management says the new plant was running at about 25-30% of capacity; ramp-up expected from mid-to-end November 2026, with about 50% utilisation of the new plant by fiscal year-end.
H1 capex about INR79 crores; FY27 capex guidance about INR175 crores; FY28 about INR50-70 crores.
HFFR capacity to be doubled to about 20,000 tons by end of the year.
BESS plant under construction; management says it will not secure firm orders until the plant goes live, targeted for Q1 FY28.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand described as resilient; Q2 was seasonally weak because of monsoon. Management expects domestic demand to improve from this quarter.

Export volumes were hit by Middle East disruption. Sea freight rose from about $10-20 per ton to $300-350 per ton in some lanes, and transit times and vessel frequency became unstable. Management expects normalisation by end-Q3 or early Q4 FY27.
Company is a cost-plus supplier to most domestic customers, passing through price changes with a lag of 5-7 days. Export contracts are mostly spot, with a lag of 15-20 days.
Q2 EBITDA per ton of about INR17,000 included war-risk premium in exports for part of the quarter, which management calls unsustainable.
Average selling price rose to about INR192 per ton in H1 FY27 from about INR145 a year earlier. Management said the increase is driving higher debtors.
Management said new entrants, including the Aditya Birla Group, are present in Wires & Cable. It declined to give customer-specific data and said growth came from adding new customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term EBITDA margin guidance, given that margins are squeezed despite strong top-line growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to EBITDA per ton, about INR17,000 in Q2 versus INR15,500 a year earlier and an FY26 average of about INR15,700. The sustainable range is INR14,000 to INR17,000, and percentage margins should improve once raw material prices fall after the war.

qa_highlights.question: How will utilisation ramp up, and what are the incremental ROCE and ROE expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation was about 63% against 81% a year earlier, and the new plant was at about 25-30%. Ramp-up starts mid-to-end November after festivals, reaching about 50% of new-plant capacity by FY-end, with XLPE demand picking up after monsoon. No ROCE or ROE figures were given.

qa_highlights.question: Is BESS revenue included in the INR5,000 crore FY30 target, and what revenue per GWh is assumed?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR5,000 crore target covers only the compounding business; BESS is additional. Management cited Chinese and Indian prices of about $80-85/kWh, implying about INR4-4.5 crores per 5 MWh container delivered in India.

qa_highlights.question: Is the volume growth guidance intact, given H1 volume growth of only 1-2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume guidance is unchanged. H1 was hit by the Middle East war and the monsoon; H2 will carry the growth. H1 volume was about 102,000 tons against an internal annual estimate of about 230,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: Will the rise in debtors and finance cost ease, and how is working capital moving?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors rose to about INR650 crores from INR400 crores, and inventory to about INR400 crores from INR250-260 crores. Management expects the Q2 finance cost of INR11.5 crores to be the FY peak, with working capital easing as prices fall.

qa_highlights.question: Is the BESS project delayed, and are there technical issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no technical issues. The timeline slipped because the state incentive policy was delayed; it was notified on 5 November 2026 and the company is now reviewing it before applying.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict keeps freight, transit times and war-risk premiums high, which pressures export volumes and margins.
Utilisation at about 63% depends on the H2 ramp-up of new PVC and XLPE capacity from mid-November.
Working capital is stretched, with debtors up to about INR650 crores and inventory up to about INR400 crores; finance cost was INR11.5 crores in Q2.
Volume growth of 10-15% for FY27 against H1 growth of only 1-2% needs to be delivered in H2.
BESS go-live is pending the state policy and has no confirmed orders; competition in BESS assembly is rising.
Margin sustainability depends on raw material prices normalising; the INR17,000 per ton figure includes temporary war-risk premium.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and on the INR5,000 crore FY30 target, but cautious on near-term margins, exports and working capital. Management repeatedly attributed the weak H1 volumes and export disruption to the Middle East war and monsoon, and sometimes answered questions indirectly, for example on customer-specific data and BESS order visibility.
